conclusion: Nonlinear photonic architectures offer a promising path toward practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: All Hilbert Spaces Are The Same: Consequences For Generalized Coordinates And Momenta
authors: S. J. van Enk And Daniel A. Steck
abstract:
Author(s): S. J. van Enk and Daniel A. Steck

Making use of the simple fact that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of given dimension are isomorphic, we show that there are just six basic ways to define generalized coordinate operators in quantum mechanics. In each case, a canonically conjugate generalized momentum operator can be defined, b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033117] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of given dimension are isomorphic, leading to only six basic ways to define generalized coordinate and momentum operators.
motivation: To understand the fundamental structure of quantum mechanics by exploring the consequences of Hilbert space isomorphism for the definition of canonical operators.
method: The authors use the mathematical fact that all separable complex Hilbert spaces of the same dimension are isomorphic to classify possible definitions of generalized coordinate operators and their conjugate momenta.
result: There are exactly six distinct ways to define generalized coordinate operators, each with a canonically conjugate momentum operator, based on the choice of basis and operator representation.
conclusion: The isomorphism of Hilbert spaces imposes strong constraints on the formulation of quantum mechanics, reducing the possible forms of canonical commutation relations to a finite set.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis is proposed, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a classical machine learning technique; quantum speedups could enable analysis of larger datasets.
method: The paper designs a quantum algorithm that computes persistent homology using quantum amplitude estimation and quantum phase estimation.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup over classical methods for certain input parameters.
conclusion: While theoretically interesting, the result is not directly aligned with the researcher's core interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to quantitative neural recording experiments.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors and demonstrate that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for preparing arbitrary n-qubit quantum states and implementing diagonal unitaries, achieving Θ(4^n) scaling with ancilla.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, as T gates are expensive to implement. Prior work left open the question of optimal scaling.
method: The authors provide a constructive algorithm using ancilla qubits and prove matching lower bounds via counting arguments and information-theoretic techniques.
result: The optimal T-count for state preparation is Θ(4^n) with ancilla, and the same scaling holds for diagonal unitaries. They also show parallel synthesis of many single-qubit unitaries at the cost of one.
conclusion: The work settles the asymptotic T-count complexity for state preparation and diagonal unitaries, with implications for resource-efficient quantum algorithms.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers who can obtain superpositions of transcripts, and previous solutions relied on commitments not known from standard assumptions.
method: The authors present a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head technique, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and construct two three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA based on the learning with errors (LWE) assumption.
result: They obtain zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA that are secure against superposition attacks, assuming LWE.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA with superposition security from standard cryptographic assumptions.

title: Quantum Mechanics On The Line With Two Origins
authors: Abhiram Sripat
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study scalar and spinorial quantum dynamics on the standard line with two origins, \[ \Ltwo=(\R_1\sqcup\R_2)/\!\sim, \qquad (x,1)\sim(x,2)\quadx\neq0, \] equipped with its identity-glued smooth structure and flat metric. We first show that the ordinary scalar theory is insensitive to the doubled origin: every continuous map from \(\Ltwo\) to a Hausdorff space factors through the quotient \(q:\Ltwo\to\R\), while, for the natural measure, \[ C^\infty(\Ltwo)\cong C^\infty(\R), \qquad L^2(\Ltwo)\cong L^2(\R). \] Accordingly, the natural scalar free Hamiltonian is unitarily equivalent to the free Laplacian on \(\R\). The doubled origin remains visible, however, in the spinor line associated with the nontrivial spin structure. The oriented flat structure on \(\Ltwo\) admits two spin structures, distinguished by the relative transition sign on the two connected components of the chart overlap. For the nontrivial structure, these signs are opposite. This forces every continuous global spinor section to vanish at both origins and every smooth section to vanish there to infinite order. The associated first-order operator \[ -i\,{\mathrm dx} \] on compactly supported smooth twisted sections is symmetric but not essentially self-adjoint: its deficiency indices are \((1,1)\), and a self-adjoint first-order evolution requires an additional transmission condition at the origin. The natural positive quadratic form associated with the flat twisted structure instead yields the direct sum of two Dirichlet half-line Laplacians and hence perfect reflection. Thus the ordinary scalar theory does not detect the doubled origin, whereas the nontrivially glued spinor line does, although the spin structure alone does not determine a unique unitary transmission law.
tldr: This paper studies quantum mechanics on a line with two origins, showing that scalar theory is insensitive to the doubled origin while spinor theory with a nontrivial spin structure reveals it.
motivation: To understand how topological features of a manifold affect quantum dynamics, specifically the doubled origin in a non-Hausdorff space.
method: Analyzes scalar and spinorial quantum dynamics on the glued line using functional analysis and spin structure classification.
result: Scalar theory is equivalent to standard line; spinor theory with nontrivial spin structure forces vanishing at origins and yields deficiency indices (1,1) for the Dirac operator.
conclusion: The doubled origin is invisible to scalar fields but detectable via spinor fields, though the spin structure alone does not determine a unique unitary transmission law.

title: Astroid Spinodal Boundary In Phase-Based Ising Machines
authors: Nikhil Shukla Malihe Farasat
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillator Ising machines (OIMs) and dynamical Ising machines (DIMs) encode binary spins in phase states stabilized by second-harmonic injection (SHI). In a coupled network, the competition between SHI and the instantaneous local network field reshapes each oscillator's conditional energy landscape. We show that this competition drives a transition between monostable and bistable regimes through an astroid spinodal boundary. Near this boundary, the barrier scales as [MATH] at generic smooth points and as [MATH] at the longitudinal cusp. OIMs and DIMs obey the same spinodal geometry, with their conditional landscapes related by a reversal of the transverse field. Finally, the first-harmonic conditional landscape is mathematically equivalent, up to an additive constant, to the Stoner--Wohlfarth energy of a uniaxial magnetic particle.
tldr: This paper analyzes the spinodal boundary in oscillator-based Ising machines, revealing a universal astroid geometry.
motivation: Understanding the transition between monostable and bistable regimes in phase-based Ising machines is crucial for optimizing their performance.
method: The authors derive the conditional energy landscape for coupled oscillators with second-harmonic injection and analyze the barrier scaling near the spinodal boundary.
result: They show that the competition between injection and network field creates an astroid spinodal boundary, with barrier scaling as (Δ)^(3/2) at smooth points and (Δ)^2 at the cusp.
conclusion: Oscillator Ising machines and dynamical Ising machines share the same spinodal geometry, and the first-harmonic landscape is equivalent to the Stoner-Wohlfarth energy of a uniaxial magnetic particle.

title: Hardware-Aware Qubo Reformulation Of Constrained Binary Optimization Via The Walsh-Fourier Transform
authors: Loong Kuan Lee, Harsha Nagarajan, Thore Gerlach, Sascha M\"ucke, Ragavi Krishnamoorthy, Nico Piatkowski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel slack-free, penalty-based framework for reformulating constrained binary optimization as Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) on near-term quantum annealing hardware. Given a user-chosen penalty function that most naturally captures a constraint---typically non-quadratic, such as a Heaviside-function surrogate---and a target probability measure over the Boolean hypercube, our method returns the weighted least-squares projection of the chosen penalty function onto the subspace spanned by linear and quadratic Walsh--Fourier characters that correspond to physically realizable couplings on the target hardware graph. Within this restricted family, the resulting quadratic surrogate is uniquely and optimally determined by the normal equations: unlike state-of-the-art approaches, it introduces no per-constraint penalty coefficients to tune and avoids dense all-pairs couplings by construction. Two practical consequences follow. First, the projected penalty respects device connectivity, reducing chain lengths and physical-qubit overhead after minor embedding. Second, we show empirically that this hardware-native surrogate can outperform denser full-pairwise projections, despite being drawn from a strictly smaller approximation space. This advantage widens once the QUBO is embedded and sampled on quantum annealers, yielding samples with the lowest worst-case and mean objective gaps compared to unbalanced penalization and a hardware-blind projection onto all quadratic terms.
tldr: A hardware-aware method to reformulate constrained binary optimization as QUBO using Walsh-Fourier projection, tailored for quantum annealing hardware.
motivation: Current QUBO reformulations introduce many penalty coefficients and dense couplings, leading to poor embedding on quantum annealers. The authors aim to produce a slack-free, penalty-based QUBO that respects hardware connectivity.
method: They project a user-chosen penalty function onto the subspace spanned by linear and quadratic Walsh-Fourier characters that correspond to physically realizable couplings on the target hardware graph, solving the normal equations to obtain the optimal quadratic surrogate.
result: The hardware-native surrogate reduces chain lengths and physical-qubit overhead, and empirically outperforms denser full-pairwise projections in terms of worst-case and mean objective gaps after embedding and sampling.
conclusion: The proposed framework yields better quality solutions on quantum annealers by avoiding dense couplings and eliminating the need for per-constraint penalty tuning.

title: Non-Hermitian Random Matrix Theory Of Jamming In Active Disordered Media
authors: Hisao Hayakawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theoretical framework for the mechanics of active jammed systems based on non-Hermitian random matrix theory. Starting from a microscopic model of active particles with non-reciprocal interactions, we formulate the linearized dynamical matrix as a non-Hermitian perturbation of a Wishart ensemble describing the passive contact network. Using Girko's Hermitization together with the self-consistent Born approximation, we derive a self-consistent equation for the low-frequency resolvent based on the full Marchenko--Pastur distribution. We show that active non-reciprocity regularizes the soft-mode divergence at the jamming transition, leading to a scaling law for the mechanical compliance. We further establish a crossover between perturbative and activity-dominated regimes and propose a corresponding scaling form near the active jamming point.
tldr: Develops a non-Hermitian random matrix theory for jamming in active disordered media.
motivation: To understand the mechanical properties of active jammed systems with non-reciprocal interactions.
method: Formulates the linearized dynamical matrix as a non-Hermitian perturbation of a Wishart ensemble and uses Girko's Hermitization with self-consistent Born approximation.
result: Shows that active non-reciprocity regularizes the soft-mode divergence at the jamming transition, leading to a scaling law for mechanical compliance.
conclusion: Establishes a crossover between perturbative and activity-dominated regimes near the active jamming point.

title: Addressing Rotational Motion On Gravitational Waves Detectors
authors: Jian Liu Chiara Di Fronzo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rotational components of Earth's seismic motion are one of the major contributions to limit the sensitivity of terrestrial gravitational-wave detectors at frequencies below 10 Hz. The fundamental challenges lie in understanding the angular degrees of freedom of seismic motion and how they can be accurately measured. These are both crucial steps for developing an adequate control system to suppress seismic motion and maintaining resonance in the detector cavities. This review shows why the rotational ground motion limits the detector's sensitivity and gives an overview of the technological achievements of the last decade on both the sensing and control systems sides. Perspectives on future developments in the field are also briefly illustrated.
tldr: A review of rotational ground motion effects on gravitational wave detectors and sensing/control technologies.
motivation: Rotational seismic motion limits detector sensitivity below 10 Hz; understanding and measuring it is crucial for control systems.
method: Review of recent technological achievements in sensing and control of rotational ground motion.
result: Overview of how rotational motion affects sensitivity and summary of sensing/control advances.
conclusion: Future developments in rotational motion sensing and control are needed to improve detector performance.

title: Quantum Random Number Generation Using Spatial Quantum Noise Of Light
authors: Ashok Kumar Mohamed Armoon Shaliq
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating high-speed, verifiable random numbers is a fundamental requirement for cryptography, large-scale stochastic simulations, and secure quantum communication. Here, we present a robust quantum random number generator that utilizes the spatial distribution of quantum fluctuations captured by an electron-multiplying charge-coupled device operated in high-speed kinetic mode. Through rigorous detector calibration and shot-noise analysis, we characterize the spatial quantum noise obtained from the spatial intensity fluctuations of the coherent states of light. Such quantum noise serves as a high-entropy source, enabling an instantaneous random bit generation rate of 5.92 Gbps without algorithmic randomness extraction in the present configuration. The sustained output rate is, however, limited to 7.5 Mbps by the bandwidth of the serial electronic readout. The generated sequences successfully pass the NIST SP 800-22 and Marsaglia Diehard statistical test suites, confirming the high quality and unpredictability of the entropy source.
tldr: A quantum random number generator using spatial quantum noise of light achieves high-speed random bit generation.
motivation: High-speed, verifiable random numbers are essential for cryptography and simulations; existing QRNGs often require complex setups or post-processing.
method: Spatial intensity fluctuations of coherent states are captured by an EMCCD in kinetic mode; shot-noise analysis extracts quantum noise as entropy source.
result: Instantaneous bit rate of 5.92 Gbps without extraction; sustained rate 7.5 Mbps limited by readout; sequences pass NIST and Diehard tests.
conclusion: The approach demonstrates a robust, high-speed QRNG using spatial quantum noise, but the sustained rate is constrained by hardware.

title: The Code Distortion Problem
authors: Huck Bennett, Matthew Fox, Bryant Morrell
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two linear error-correcting codes [MATH] are called linearly equivalent if there is a linear isometry mapping [MATH] to [MATH]. In this work, we generalize the notion of linear equivalence and study the minimum distortion [MATH] of a linear mapping between codes [MATH], which quantifies how similar [MATH] and [MATH] are. We introduce and study the Code Distortion Problem (CDP), which asks to find a minimum distortion mapping between two input codes [MATH] and [MATH]. CDP generalizes the Linear Code Equivalence Problem (LCE), which is essentially the special case of CDP where [MATH] and which is well-studied because of its role in cryptography. We prove that (decisional) CDP is [MATH]-hard to approximate to within any constant factor, and that it is in [MATH]. We also give a single-exponential-time [MATH]-approximation algorithm for CDP, where [MATH] is the dimension of the input codes. Furthermore, we give a single-exponential-time [MATH]-approximation algorithm for a natural special case of CDP, and we show that our analysis is tight in this case. We use techniques from analogous work on the Lattice Distortion Problem (LDP) by Bennett, Dadush, and Stephens-Davidowitz (ESA, 2016). We also introduce or study a number of additional concepts that might be of independent interest. These include an adaptation of the celebrated reduction of Goldreich, Micciancio, Safra, and Seifert (IPL, 1999) from the Shortest Vector Problem (SVP) to the Closest Vector Problem (CVP) on lattices to the analogous problems on codes; successive minima bases for codes; and the matrix [MATH] "norm" on subspaces.
tldr: This paper studies the Code Distortion Problem, a generalization of linear code equivalence, focusing on computational hardness and approximation algorithms.
motivation: The problem generalizes the Linear Code Equivalence Problem, which is important in cryptography, and aims to quantify similarity between linear codes.
method: The authors prove NP-hardness of approximation for CDP, provide an exponential-time approximation algorithm, and adapt techniques from lattice problems.
result: CDP is NP-hard to approximate within any constant factor, and a single-exponential-time O(√n)-approximation algorithm is given.
conclusion: The work establishes foundational complexity results for CDP and introduces new concepts like successive minima bases for codes.

title: Two Instances Of Chaos In Deterministic And Quantum Dynamical Systems
authors: Andrea Ulliana
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This thesis consists of two distinct projects situated in the areas of smooth dynamics and spectral theory, respectively. They are united by a common interest in mechanisms of chaos and statistical behavior in classical and quantum dynamical systems. The first concerns smooth dynamics. We prove that all ergodic linear automorphisms of the N-dimensional torus with two-dimensional center are stably ergodic, including all ergodic automorphisms in dimensions [MATH] and [MATH] . This generalizes a previous result of Rodriguez-Hertz, which required an additional algebraic condition on the characteristic polynomial of the linear automorphism. The second project deals with spectral theory of Schr\"odinger operators. We prove that delocalization of most eigenvectors is topologically common in the space of deterministic Schr\"odinger Operators on a given large finite graph, provided that the IDS satisfies a suitable regularity condition. This result generalizes a recent theorem of Avila and Damanik. We also describe a flexible family of graphs satisfying our criterion, by proving a variant of the Thouless formula.
tldr: The thesis studies ergodicity of torus automorphisms and delocalization of eigenvectors in Schrödinger operators, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand mechanisms of chaos in classical and quantum dynamical systems.
method: Proves stable ergodicity for linear automorphisms with two-dimensional center and shows delocalization is generic for Schrödinger operators on large finite graphs.
result: Generalizes prior results on stable ergodicity and delocalization.
conclusion: The work contributes to smooth dynamics and spectral theory, not to the user's research directions.

title: Learning The Word Problem: Geodesic Lengths And Cryptographic Applications
authors: Elisabeth Fink
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Word Problem has been a subject of intensive mathematical study for over a century, initially driving advances in combinatorial group theory and more recently emerging as a foundational hardness assumption in post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While generally undecidable, several families of infinite non-abelian groups exhibit solvable or algorithmically fast word problems, making them attractive platforms for cryptographic design. This paper introduces WPNet, a novel Graph Neural Network architecture capable of solving the Word Problem heuristically, which is demonstrated on the Baumslag-Solitar group [MATH] and on an Artin group. By mapping unreduced words to dynamic graph structures, the model learns to cluster algebraically equivalent elements in a continuous embedding space, effectively identifying the geodesic representative of a word without executing discrete reduction steps. As an application, a model variant is developed that can predict the geodesic length of an unreduced word in both groups. To demonstrate the cryptographic severity of this structural leakage, WPNet is successfully deployed against the Wagner-Magyarik public-key cryptosystem.
tldr: This paper uses graph neural networks to heuristically solve the word problem in infinite non-abelian groups and applies it to break a post-quantum cryptosystem.
motivation: The word problem is a classic undecidable problem in group theory, but some groups have efficient solutions; the paper aims to learn these solutions heuristically and assess cryptographic implications.
method: A Graph Neural Network (WPNet) is trained to map unreduced words to graph structures and learn to identify geodesic representatives and predict geodesic lengths without explicit reduction steps.
result: WPNet successfully solves the word problem for Baumslag-Solitar and Artin groups, and predicts geodesic lengths, which is used to attack the Wagner-Magyarik public-key cryptosystem.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that machine learning can exploit structural properties of groups to break cryptographic assumptions, highlighting risks for post-quantum cryptography based on combinatorial group theory.

title: Upper Bounds For The Monotone Rank Of The Unique Disjointness Matrix
authors: Igor S. Sergeev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.27014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that the [MATH]-rank (covering rank) of the [MATH] unique disjointness matrix is [MATH], hence the known lower bound [MATH] turns out to be essentially tight. By the way, an upper bound [MATH] is obtained for the [MATH]-rank (partition rank) of this matrix.
tldr: This paper proves tight upper bounds on the monotone rank and partition rank of the unique disjointness matrix, a combinatorial communication complexity problem.
motivation: The unique disjointness matrix is a fundamental object in communication complexity, and understanding its rank measures has implications for lower bounds in various computational models.
method: The author uses combinatorial and algebraic arguments to derive upper bounds on the covering rank (monotone rank) and partition rank of the matrix.
result: The monotone rank of the unique disjointness matrix is shown to be O(2^{n/2}), matching the known lower bound, and an upper bound O(2^{n/2}) is also obtained for the partition rank.
conclusion: The results essentially settle the monotone rank of the unique disjointness matrix and provide new insights into its partition rank.

title: Reply To: Conductance Measurements Cannot Distinguish Crossed Andreev Reflection From Elastic Co-tunnelling In Normal–superconductor–normal Junctions
authors: Junya Feng

method: The paper provides a theoretical analysis showing that both processes produce identical conductance signatures, making them indistinguishable via conductance alone.

authors: Michael E. Ziebel

motivation: To explore superconductivity in a layered van der Waals material under pressure, which may reveal new physics related to dimensionality and Kondo interactions.
method: The authors applied pressure to CeSiI and measured its superconducting properties.
result: Superconductivity was observed under pressure in CeSiI.
conclusion: CeSiI offers a new platform for studying the interplay of dimensionality and Kondo physics in superconductivity.

title: Conductance Measurements Cannot Distinguish Crossed Andreev Reflection From Elastic Co-tunnelling In Normal–superconductor–normal Junctions
authors: E. S. Tikhonov
V. S. Khrapai

tldr: The paper shows that conductance measurements cannot distinguish crossed Andreev reflection from elastic co-tunnelling in normal-superconductor-normal junctions.

authors: Tong Shi

authors: Ruben van Assche

title: Emergence Of Fermi-liquid And Bcs Physics In Overdoped Cuprates
authors: B. J. Ramshaw

tldr: This paper argues that observed behaviors in overdoped cuprates can be explained by substitutional disorder in a d-wave superconductor, rather than requiring non-Fermi-liquid physics.
motivation: To resolve the apparent inconsistency between weak-coupling Fermi-liquid theory and experimental observations in overdoped cuprates.
method: The authors present a perspective based on theoretical arguments and analysis of substitutional disorder effects in d-wave superconductors.
result: They propose that in the disorder-free limit, a weak-coupling Fermi-liquid-based BCS description is possible.

title: Universality Emerging In A Universality: Derivation Of The Ericson Transition In Stochastic Quantum Scattering And Experimental Validation
authors: Simon Köhnes, Jiongning Che, Barbara Dietz, And Thomas Guhr
abstract:
Author(s): Simon Köhnes, Jiongning Che, Barbara Dietz, and Thomas Guhr

At lower energies, the resonances in scattering experiments are often isolated. In quantum chaotic many-body, disordered, or generically stochastic systems, the resonances overlap at larger energies. Eventually, the Ericson regime is reached in which the cross section behaves like a random function.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050403] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives the Ericson transition in stochastic quantum scattering and validates it experimentally, focusing on resonance overlap in chaotic systems.
motivation: To understand the transition from isolated to overlapping resonances in quantum chaotic scattering, known as the Ericson regime.
method: The authors derive a universal formula for the Ericson transition using random matrix theory and validate it with experimental data from microwave cavities.

method: Continuum model of gapped monolayer graphene with substrate interaction, solving for single-electron bound states.
result: Theoretical characterization of bound states and their magnetic field dependence.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for nonlocal qubits in graphene quantum dots, but does not directly address quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

authors: J. G. Rojas-Briseño, A. Astrain-Ortega, Y. Y. Huamani-Tapia, S. Molina-Valdovinos, And I. Rodríguez-Vargas

Several studies propose two-dimensional (2D) materials as candidates for spintronic and valleytronic devices. The capability to access two well-defined spin-valley polarization states is the main factor for a good spin-valleytronic device. Each 2D material possesses certain characteristics that can …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065429] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-valley polarization in ferromagnetic MoS2 monolayer junctions for spintronic and valleytronic applications.
motivation: Two-dimensional materials are promising for spintronic and valleytronic devices, and accessing well-defined spin-valley polarization states is crucial.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations or transport simulations to investigate spin-valley polarization in 1T'-MoS2 monolayer junctions.
result: They find that the junctions exhibit significant spin-valley polarization, which can be controlled by external means.
conclusion: The material shows potential for use in spin-valleytronic devices, but the work is primarily materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Disorder Information From Conductance In Quantum Mesoscopic Transport: A Statistical Approach To The Quantum Inverse Problem And The Scope Of Optimal Solutions

Inferring properties of microscopic disorder potential from macroscopic transport measurements is a formidable challenging inverse problem in the low-dimensional nanostructures, particularly when the disorder is dynamic and experimentally uncontrolled. In this work, we investigate the inverse proble…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065431] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses conductance measurements to infer disorder properties in quantum mesoscopic transport via a statistical inverse problem approach.
motivation: Inferring microscopic disorder from macroscopic transport is challenging, especially for dynamic disorder in low-dimensional nanostructures.
method: The authors develop a statistical framework to solve the quantum inverse problem, relating conductance fluctuations to disorder parameters.
result: They demonstrate that optimal solutions can be obtained under certain conditions, providing a method to extract disorder information from transport data.
conclusion: The approach offers a way to characterize disorder in mesoscopic systems, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Zitterbewegung Velocity In Semiclassical Electron Dynamics
authors: Dimitrie Culcer
abstract:
Author(s): Dimitrie Culcer

itterbewegung, the trembling motion caused by interband coherence, is usually viewed as a purely quantum effect. Here, the author shows that it also has a natural place in semiclassical electron dynamics as an additional velocity term. This term explains the electric-field-induced position shift of Bloch electrons and reveals a direct connection to the minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020305] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that Zitterbewegung, typically a quantum effect, appears as a velocity term in semiclassical electron dynamics, explaining electric-field-induced position shifts and connecting to minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the role of interband coherence in semiclassical electron dynamics and its observable consequences.
method: Theoretical derivation incorporating Zitterbewegung as an additional velocity term in the semiclassical equations of motion.
result: The Zitterbewegung velocity term accounts for electric-field-induced position shifts of Bloch electrons and relates to the minimum conductivity of massless Dirac fermions.
conclusion: Zitterbewegung has a natural semiclassical interpretation and is not purely quantum, with implications for transport in Dirac materials.

title: Pseudo-Goldstone Mode In Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe: High-field Electron Spin Resonance Studies

[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020407] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.

motivation: Altermagnetic materials have attracted recent attention, and understanding their low-energy spin dynamics is important.
method: The authors perform electron spin resonance spectroscopy in high magnetic fields to investigate the spin-wave Goldstone mode.
result: In a specific geometry, the Goldstone mode acquires a gap controlled by the magnetic field, and the resonance linewidth follows a universal 1/T behavior.
conclusion: Thermally assisted magnon-magnon collisions are the key magnetic relaxation mechanism in α-MnTe.

title: Magnetocubic And Magnetolinear Dependence Observed In The In-plane Anomalous Hall Magnet ${\mathrm{EuCd}}_{2}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{2}$
authors: Ayano Nakamura, Shinichi Nishihaya, Mitsuru Akaki, Motoi Kimata, Kenta Sudo, Yuki Deguchi, Hsiang Lee, Tadashi Yoneda, Markus Kriener, Masaki Kondo, Hiroaki Ishizuka, Masashi Tokunaga, And Masaki Uchida

The Hall effect under in-plane magnetic field has emerged as a sensitive probe of quantum geometric properties in solids. In trigonal systems, the in-plane anomalous Hall effect (AHE) originates from unconventional off-diagonal coupling between the magnetic field and the Hall vector on the principal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051112] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of magnetocubic and magnetolinear contributions to the in-plane anomalous Hall effect in the magnetic semimetal EuCd2Sb2.
motivation: To understand the origin of in-plane anomalous Hall effect in trigonal systems and its relation to quantum geometric properties.
method: Transport measurements under in-plane magnetic field on single crystals of EuCd2Sb2, analyzing the angular and field dependence of the Hall resistivity.
result: The in-plane anomalous Hall effect exhibits both magnetocubic (∝ M^3) and magnetolinear (∝ M) contributions, with the cubic term dominating at low fields.
conclusion: The observed behavior is attributed to the interplay of Berry curvature and magnetic texture, providing insight into the anomalous Hall effect in trigonal magnets.

title: Topological Dislocation Response In Elementary Semiconductors
authors: Yuteng Zhou, Alexandre Chaduteau, And Frank Schindler
abstract:

We study elementary semiconductors and insulators that are symmetric under spatial inversion: silicon, diamond, germanium, and black phosphorene. These materials are ideal candidates for realizing obstructed atomic insulators, which differ from trivial atomic insulators by a quantized spatial shift …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051302] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological dislocation responses in elementary semiconductors, focusing on obstructed atomic insulators and quantized spatial shifts.
motivation: To understand the topological properties of common semiconductors and identify obstructed atomic insulators.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis of silicon, diamond, germanium, and black phosphorene.
result: These materials exhibit obstructed atomic insulator phases with quantized spatial shifts.
conclusion: Elementary semiconductors can host nontrivial topological phases beyond conventional topological insulators.

title: Classifying The Topology Of Finite Chiral Structures Using Complete Matchings
authors: Maxine M. Mccarthy And D. M. Whittaker
abstract:
Author(s): Maxine M. McCarthy and D. M. Whittaker

Here, the authors propose a general framework to understand the relationship between structural connectivity and topological classification. Their approach can be applied to arbitrary finite chiral structures that may have a highly complex connectivity and lack a natural bulk description, in contrast to most classification schemes. Furthermore, by splitting the structure into sections, they show that many systems exhibit a richer classification than predicted with a purely symmetry-based approach. Tied to the topological phases they classify, unusual localization and transport phenomena are predicted and experimentally demonstrated.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024210] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a framework to classify the topology of finite chiral structures using complete matchings, predicting localization and transport phenomena.
motivation: Existing topological classification schemes often require a bulk description, which is not applicable to finite chiral structures with complex connectivity.
method: The authors develop a general framework based on splitting the structure into sections and using complete matchings to classify topology.
result: The approach reveals a richer classification than symmetry-based methods and predicts unusual localization and transport phenomena, which are experimentally demonstrated.
conclusion: The framework provides a new way to understand topology in finite systems without a natural bulk limit.

title: Suppression Of Magnetism In ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$ Under External Pressure
authors: A. Chmeruk, D. Jones, R. Dwadasi, J. Ebad-Allah, F. Beiuşeanu, F. Schilberth, M. A. Kassem, U. Schade, A. Veber, L. Puskar, Y. Tabata, T. Waki, H. Nakamura, C. A. Kuntscher, A. Östlin, And L. Chioncel
abstract:

Magnetic materials with nontrivial band topology combine key concepts of modern solid-state physics and are expected to broaden the range of emergent quantum phases. At the same time, external pressure has proven to be a viable tool in manipulating the band topology and magnetism. Using first-principle simulations combined with optical spectroscopy measurements, the authors show here how the correlation effects are largely responsible for the suppression of the ferromagnetic state in a prototypical Weyl semimetal Co
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024423] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the suppression of ferromagnetism in Co3Sn2S2 under pressure using first-principles simulations and optical spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand how external pressure affects the interplay between band topology and magnetism in a Weyl semimetal.
method: Combined density functional theory (DFT) simulations with optical spectroscopy measurements under varying pressure.
result: Correlation effects are largely responsible for the suppression of the ferromagnetic state under pressure.
conclusion: Pressure can tune magnetic and topological properties, but the study is primarily condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unified Machine-learning Framework For Structural Reconstruction And Flat-band Formation In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{MoSi}}_{2}{\mathrm{N}}_{4}$
authors: Jiamin Luo, Chunhui Li, Lei Shan, And Long Cheng

Here, we develop a unified machine-learning framework that integrates machine-learning interatomic potentials with Hamiltonian graph neural network…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045432] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: A machine-learning framework for structural reconstruction and flat-band formation in twisted bilayer MoSi2N4.
motivation: Flat-band engineering in moiré materials is sensitive to twist angles, but accurate large-scale simulations are computationally prohibitive.
method: Integrates machine-learning interatomic potentials with Hamiltonian graph neural networks to predict atomic structure and electronic properties.
result: The framework enables efficient and accurate prediction of structural relaxation and flat-band formation at various twist angles.
conclusion: Provides a unified computational tool for studying moiré materials, bypassing expensive first-principles calculations.

title: Conventional And Practical Metallic Superconductivity Arising From Repulsive Coulomb Coupling
authors: Sankar Das Sarma, Jay D. Sau, Yi-Ting Tu, And Shuyang Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sankar Das Sarma, Jay D. Sau, Yi-Ting Tu, and Shuyang Wang

A concrete question is discussed: Can there be conventional [MATH]-wave superconductivity (SC) in regular three-dimensional (3D) (or 2D) metals, i.e., electrons in a jellium background, interacting via the standard Coulomb coupling? We are interested in “practical” SC that can in principle be observed …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055202] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates whether conventional s-wave superconductivity can arise from repulsive Coulomb coupling in three-dimensional metals.
motivation: To address the long-standing question of whether purely repulsive interactions can lead to superconductivity in simple metals, which has implications for understanding unconventional superconductivity.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly numerical calculations to study the pairing instability in a jellium model with Coulomb interactions.
result: They find that conventional s-wave superconductivity is possible under certain conditions, providing a concrete example of repulsive-induced pairing.
conclusion: Repulsive Coulomb interactions can indeed give rise to conventional superconductivity in three-dimensional metals, offering insights into the mechanisms of superconductivity.

title: Hybrid-order Topology In Two-dimensional Nonsymmorphic Antiferromagnets
authors: Wei Xiong, Zi-Ming Wang, Xin-Mei Wei, Rui Wang, And Dong-Hui Xu

Utilizing a generic antiferromagnetic Dirac model with a symmetry-allowed, momentum-dependent spin-density-wave mass, we show that a single bulk insulating phase exhibits distinct topological bound…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065137] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically demonstrates hybrid-order topology in a two-dimensional nonsymmorphic antiferromagnet.
motivation: To explore novel topological phases in antiferromagnetic materials with nonsymmorphic symmetry.
method: Using a generic antiferromagnetic Dirac model with a symmetry-allowed, momentum-dependent spin-density-wave mass.
result: A single bulk insulating phase exhibits distinct topological boundary states of different orders.
conclusion: Hybrid-order topology can exist in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic antiferromagnets, expanding the understanding of topological phases.

title: Dirac Topology, Anomalous Hall Response, And Giant Magnetoresistance In The Carrier-compensated Altermagnetic Semimetal NiS

T…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L051111] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure and transport properties of the altermagnetic semimetal NiS using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand the interplay between topology, magnetism, and lattice dynamics in NiS, which exhibits altermagnetism and carrier compensation.
method: Combines density-functional theory, Berry-curvature analysis, semiclassical Boltzmann transport, and atomistic spin dynamics.
result: NiS is identified as a compensated altermagnetic semimetal with Dirac topology, anomalous Hall response, and giant magnetoresistance.
conclusion: The material's properties arise from the intrinsic coupling of topology and magnetism, offering a platform for spintronic applications.

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014209] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-momentum relaxation and coherent backscattering of matter waves under SU(2) gauge fields in disordered potentials.
motivation: To understand the interplay between gauge fields and disorder in mesoscopic systems, which is relevant for spintronics and cold atom experiments.
method: The authors derive the disorder-averaged density matrix using weak-localization theory and analyze time- and momentum-resolved dynamics.
result: They find that uniform SU(2) gauge fields modify the coherent backscattering peak and spin relaxation rates.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum transport in the presence of non-Abelian gauge fields, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Percolation-driven Ferromagnetism In A Dilute Magnetic Topological Insulator
authors: Farhan Islam, Santanu Pakhira, Deborah L. Schlagel, Dhurba R. Jaishi, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Thomas Heitmann, David C. Johnston, Robert J. Mcqueeney, And David Vaknin

motivation: To understand the emergence of long-range ferromagnetic order in a dilute magnetic topological insulator, which is relevant for spintronics and topological quantum computing.
method: Single-crystal neutron scattering and magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on the dilute magnetic topological insulator.
result: Long-range ferromagnetic order emerges below T_C = 12 K, driven by percolation of magnetic moments.
conclusion: The ferromagnetic order in this dilute magnetic topological insulator is percolation-driven, providing insight into magnetic ordering in such systems.

title: Anomalous Diffusion And Effective Shear Modulus In A Semisolid Membrane
authors: Vikash Pandey And Dhrubaditya Mitra
abstract:
Author(s): Vikash Pandey and Dhrubaditya Mitra

From the perspective of physical properties, the cell membrane is an exotic two-dimensional material that has a dual nature: it exhibits characteristics of fluids, i.e., lipid molecules show lateral diffusion, while also demonstrating properties of solids, evidenced by a nonzero shear modulus. We co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014411] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anomalous diffusion and effective shear modulus in a semisolid membrane, focusing on biophysical properties of cell membranes.
motivation: Cell membranes exhibit both fluid and solid properties; understanding their mechanical and diffusive behavior is important for biophysics.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or simulations to analyze diffusion and shear modulus in a semisolid membrane system.
result: The paper reports anomalous diffusion and a nonzero effective shear modulus, characterizing the dual nature of the membrane.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the physical properties of cell membranes, but the work is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Free-fermionic And Free-parafermionic Multispin Quantum Chains With Nonhomogeneous Interacting Ranges
authors: Francisco C. Alcaraz
abstract:

A large family of multispin interacting one-dimensional quantum spin models with [MATH] symmetry and a free-particle eigenspectra are known in the literature. They are free-fermionic ([MATH]) and free-parafermionic ([MATH]) quantum chains. The essential ingredient that implies the free-particle spectr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014146] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies free-fermionic and free-parafermionic multispin quantum chains with nonhomogeneous interaction ranges, focusing on exact solvability and free-particle spectra.
motivation: To generalize known families of exactly solvable quantum spin models with free-particle spectra to cases with nonhomogeneous interaction ranges, which are less understood.
method: The author constructs a family of multispin interacting quantum chains with Z_n symmetry and shows they have free-particle eigenspectra by mapping to free-fermionic or free-parafermionic systems.
result: Exact solutions are obtained for these models, demonstrating free-particle spectra despite nonhomogeneous interactions.
conclusion: The work extends the class of exactly solvable quantum spin chains, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems as defined in the research interests.

For ordinary (dyadic) networks, by using the generating function technique and stochastic simulations, we show that the relationship between the Pearson assortativity coefficient $r…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014313] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies percolation thresholds in correlated networks and hypergraphs under random node failures.
motivation: Understanding network robustness is important for real-world systems, but the paper focuses on classical network theory without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use generating function techniques and stochastic simulations to analyze assortative and disassortative mixing effects on percolation thresholds.
result: They find nonmonotonic behavior of the percolation threshold as a function of the correlation parameter.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical network science but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

Through simulation…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012202] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies scaling laws and relaxation rates at first-order desynchronization transitions in the Kuramoto model.
motivation: Understanding critical phenomena in synchronization transitions is important, but the paper focuses on classical coupled oscillators without quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: Numerical simulations of the Kuramoto model are used to analyze scaling behavior near first-order desynchronization.
result: The authors find scaling laws and relaxation rates that differ from second-order transitions.
conclusion: The work contributes to classical synchronization theory but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Self-organized Model For The Flicker Noise In Interacting Two-dimensional Electron Gas
authors: Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, And Vadood Adami
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Pirgholi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi, and Vadood Adami

We investigate self-organized criticality in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) by introducing a lattice-based model that incorporates electron-electron interactions through the concept of coherence length. Our numerical simulations demonstrate that in the strongly interacting regime, the system …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014141] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies self-organized criticality and flicker noise in a 2D electron gas with electron-electron interactions, using a lattice model and numerical simulations.
motivation: Understanding the origin of 1/f noise in interacting electron systems is a long-standing problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A lattice-based model incorporating coherence length to capture electron-electron interactions is simulated numerically to study self-organized criticality.
result: In the strongly interacting regime, the system exhibits self-organized criticality and power-law noise spectra characteristic of flicker noise.
conclusion: The model provides a possible mechanism for flicker noise in 2DEG based on self-organized criticality.

title: Spectral Statistics And Localization Properties Of A ${\mathrm{C}}_{3}$-symmetric Billiard
authors: Matic Orel And Marko Robnik
abstract:

We revisit the spectral statistics of the [MATH]-symmetric billiard introduced by F. Leyvraz et al. [
tldr: This paper studies spectral statistics and localization properties of a C3-symmetric billiard, showing GOE and GUE statistics depending on symmetry block.
motivation: To understand quantum chaos and spectral properties in systems with discrete symmetry, revisiting a known billiard with high-resolution numerical methods.
method: High-precision numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for the C3-symmetric billiard, analyzing level spacing distributions and localization measures.
result: The system exhibits GOE statistics in the symmetric subspace and GUE statistics in the antisymmetric subspace, with intermediate localization behavior.
conclusion: The C3-symmetric billiard provides a clear example of symmetry-induced spectral statistics crossover, relevant to quantum chaos theory.

title: Stability And Interactions Of Hopfions In Confined Chiral Systems: Role Of The Background Phase
authors: Andrey O. Leonov

We present a systematic study of isolated hopfions in confined layers of chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals with strong surface anchoring and a film thickness fixed to one spiral pitch. [Phys. Rev. E 114, 015416] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies hopfions in confined chiral magnets and cholesteric liquid crystals, focusing on their stability and interactions.
motivation: Hopfions are topological solitons that may have applications in spintronics and liquid crystal devices, but their behavior in confined geometries is not well understood.
method: Numerical simulations are used to model hopfions in thin films with strong surface anchoring and fixed thickness, analyzing their structure and interactions.
result: The stability and interaction properties of hopfions depend sensitively on the background phase and confinement conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling hopfions in confined systems, which could be relevant for future device applications.

title: Beyond The Arcsine Law: Aging Statistics Of The Occupation Time In Jump Processes
authors: Arthur Plaud And Olivier Bénichou
abstract:
Author(s): Arthur Plaud and Olivier Bénichou

Occupation times quantify how long a stochastic process remains in a region, and their single-time statistics are famously given by the arcsine law for Brownian and Lévy processes. By contrast, two-time occupation statistics—which directly probe temporal correlations and aging—have resisted exact ch…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014137] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, revealing aging behavior beyond the classical arcsine law.
motivation: Occupation times are fundamental in stochastic processes, but two-time statistics—which probe temporal correlations and aging—have not been exactly characterized for jump processes.
method: The authors derive exact expressions for the joint distribution of occupation times at two different times for a class of jump processes, using renewal theory and Laplace transform methods.
result: They find that the two-time occupation statistics exhibit aging, meaning the correlation depends on the absolute times, not just the time difference, and deviate from the arcsine law.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of two-time occupation statistics in jump processes, highlighting aging effects that are absent in Brownian motion.

title: Finite-size Scaling To Resolve Spurious Multifractality In The Two-dimensional Ising Model
authors: S. Jaroszewicz, N. Mendez, Maria P. Beccar-Varela, And Maria Cristina Mariani
abstract:

In this work, we resolve th…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014139] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves spurious multifractality in the 2D Ising model using finite-size scaling.
motivation: Multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis often yields spurious multifractality in discrete spin models, contradicting theory.
method: The authors apply finite-size scaling to multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis of the 2D Ising model.
result: They show that apparent multifractality is a finite-size artifact and can be removed by proper scaling.
conclusion: Finite-size scaling is essential to avoid misinterpretation of multifractality in spin models.

title: Phenomenological Renormalization Group In Neuronal Models Near Criticality

However, it remains unclear how reliably these observed signatures indicate genuine critical behavior, as it is not we…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014310] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies phenomenological renormalization group to neuronal models to study criticality, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To test whether scale-invariant signatures in neuronal data reliably indicate genuine critical behavior.
method: The authors apply the phenomenological renormalization group (PRG) to neuronal models and analyze the resulting scaling behavior.
result: The PRG method reveals signatures of criticality, but the reliability of these signatures as indicators of genuine critical behavior remains uncertain.
conclusion: The study highlights limitations of PRG in distinguishing criticality from other scale-invariant phenomena in neuronal systems.

abstract:

The phase transition in the Vicsek model is widely believed to be associated with spontaneous symmetry breaking of the two-dimensional rotational symmetry [MATH]. In this paper, we revisit the original model introduced by Vicsek et al. [
tldr: This paper shows that the Vicsek model does not exhibit O(2) symmetry breaking, contrary to common belief.
motivation: The Vicsek model is a paradigmatic model for collective motion, and its phase transition is often attributed to spontaneous breaking of O(2) symmetry. The authors aim to correct this misconception.
method: The authors revisit the original Vicsek model, analyze its symmetries, and perform numerical simulations to demonstrate the absence of O(2) symmetry breaking.
result: They find that the ordered phase in the Vicsek model does not break O(2) symmetry; instead, the transition is of a different nature.
conclusion: The widely held belief about O(2) symmetry breaking in the Vicsek model is incorrect, and the model's phase transition requires a different theoretical explanation.

title: Ghost Imaging With Free Electron-photon Pairs
authors: Sergei Bogdanov, Alexander Preimesberger, Harsh Mishra, Dominik Hornof, Thomas Spielauer, Florian Thajer, Max Maurer, Pia Falb, Leo Stöger, Thomas Schachinger, Friedrich Bleicher, Michael S. Seifner, Isobel C. Bicket, And Philipp Haslinger
abstract:
Author(s): Sergei Bogdanov, Alexander Preimesberger, Harsh Mishra, Dominik Hornof, Thomas Spielauer, Florian Thajer, Max Maurer, Pia Falb, Leo Stöger, Thomas Schachinger, Friedrich Bleicher, Michael S. Seifner, Isobel C. Bicket, and Philipp Haslinger

Coincidence imaging, also known as ghost imaging, is a technique that exploits correlations between two particles to reconstruct information about a specimen. The particle that relays the spatial information about the object remains completely noninteracting, while the particle used to probe the obj…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033120] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ghost imaging using correlated free electron-photon pairs, where the electron interacts with the object and the photon carries the spatial information.
motivation: To extend ghost imaging to a new regime using free electrons and photons, potentially enabling imaging with reduced sample damage.
method: The authors generate correlated electron-photon pairs via inverse Compton scattering and use coincidence detection to reconstruct images from the photon signal.
result: They successfully reconstruct images of test objects using only the photon arm, with the electron arm interacting with the object.
conclusion: Ghost imaging with free electron-photon pairs is feasible and may offer advantages for imaging sensitive samples.

title: Quasicrystalline Analog Of The Haldane Model
authors: B. D. K. Burgess And N. R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): B. D. K. Burgess and N. R. Cooper

We present a model for a topological quasicrystalline system that is suitable for realization in cold atom experiments. We define the model in terms of complex momentum-space couplings that break time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and detail how it may be experimentally realized using two-photon Raman cou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033105] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quasicrystalline analog of the Haldane model with broken time-reversal symmetry, suitable for cold atom experiments.
motivation: To explore topological phases in quasicrystalline systems, which lack translational symmetry but can exhibit nontrivial topology.
method: The model is defined using complex momentum-space couplings that break time-reversal symmetry, and an experimental realization via two-photon Raman coupling in cold atoms is proposed.
result: The quasicrystalline system supports chiral edge states and a nonzero Chern number, analogous to the Haldane model.
conclusion: Quasicrystalline systems can host topological phases similar to crystalline topological insulators, and the model is experimentally feasible with current cold atom techniques.

title: Position-resolved Resonance Quantization For Lossy Cavities
authors: Lucas Weitzel, Andreas Buchleitner, And Dominik Lentrodt
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Weitzel, Andreas Buchleitner, and Dominik Lentrodt

Modern experiments in resonators are moving to ever more extreme quantum regimes, posing major challenges to established theoretical approaches, such as so-called few-mode models. While these models have driven major insights for traditional regimes, they are now hitting their limitations for highly…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033108] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for resonance quantization in lossy cavities using a position-resolved approach.
motivation: Standard few-mode models fail in extreme quantum regimes of resonators; a more accurate theoretical description is needed.
method: The authors introduce a position-resolved quantization scheme that accounts for cavity losses and mode coupling.
result: They derive quantized resonance modes that incorporate spatial dependence and dissipation, improving upon few-mode approximations.
conclusion: The position-resolved approach provides a more accurate description of quantum optical phenomena in lossy cavities, relevant for cavity QED experiments.

title: Dual Energy-differentiated Topological Transition In Artificial Red Phosphorus Chains
authors: Vít Jakubský, B. Manjarrez-Montañez, Rafael A. Méndez-Sánchez, And Yonatan Betancur-Ocampo
abstract:
Author(s): Vít Jakubský, B. Manjarrez-Montañez, Rafael A. Méndez-Sánchez, and Yonatan Betancur-Ocampo

We investigate the spectral and topological properties of an atomic chain of red phosphorus. We reveal the separation of flat-band states from the rest of the system and calculate its energy bands analytically. The topological properties of the system are established through the evaluation of the Be…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033110] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological properties of an artificial red phosphorus chain, revealing flat-band separation and energy-differentiated topological transitions.
motivation: To understand the spectral and topological properties of atomic chains of red phosphorus, which may have implications for condensed matter physics.
method: Analytical calculation of energy bands and evaluation of topological invariants (e.g., Berry phase) for the atomic chain model.
result: Flat-band states are separated from the rest of the system, and energy-differentiated topological transitions are identified.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the topological nature of red phosphorus chains but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dimensional Crossover Of Bound Complexes In A Two-species Bose-Hubbard Lattice: Correlations And Dynamics
authors: Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, And Stephanie M. Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, and Stephanie M. Reimann

We study the equilibrium and nonequilibrium formation of four-particle complexes in a balanced two-species Bose-Hubbard model with repulsive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033111] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies four-particle bound complexes in a two-species Bose-Hubbard model using exact diagonalization, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the formation and dynamics of bound complexes in ultracold atomic systems is important for many-body physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Exact diagonalization of a two-species Bose-Hubbard model with repulsive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions.
result: Characterization of the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and tetramer states, and their nonequilibrium formation.
conclusion: The study provides insights into bound complexes in lattice systems, but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Pulsed Optical Injection Steering In Multistable Semiconductor Laser Arrays Under Correlated Noise
authors: Max M. Chumley And Herbert G. Winful
abstract:
Author(s): Max M. Chumley and Herbert G. Winful

We demonstrate robust programmable state preparation in small Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) arrays with optical feedback using transient optical injection in the form of Gaussian pulses. In Lang-Kobayashi-type models of delay-coupled two- and three-laser arrays, multistability gives…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033112] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable state preparation in small VCSEL arrays using pulsed optical injection under correlated noise.
motivation: To achieve robust control of multistable laser arrays for applications in optical computing and communication.
method: Uses Lang-Kobayashi-type models with delay-coupled lasers and transient Gaussian optical injection pulses.
result: Shows that pulsed injection can steer the array into desired states despite correlated noise.
conclusion: Pulsed optical injection is an effective technique for state preparation in small VCSEL arrays.

title: Spin Glass Dynamics On Complex Hardware Topologies: A Bond-correlated Percolation Approach
authors: Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, And Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz
abstract:
Author(s): Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, and Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz

Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is a central problem in statistical physics and quantum annealing. Spin glass models provide a natural framework to explore this connection, as their energy landscapes are governed by competing interactions and constraine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033099] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies using a bond-correlated percolation approach.
motivation: Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is a central problem in statistical physics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors develop a bond-correlated percolation model to analyze spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies.
result: The model captures key features of relaxation and provides insights into the role of topology in spin glass behavior.
conclusion: The bond-correlated percolation approach offers a useful framework for studying spin glass dynamics on complex networks.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, and Alessandro Toschi

By means of cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT), we study how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of the self-consistent perturbation theory in two-dimensional systems and the most relevant physical consequences associated with it, such as the CDMFT Mott transition. To this aim, we…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the associated physical consequences like the Mott transition.
method: The authors employ cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to analyze two-dimensional systems with short-range correlations.
result: They identify nonperturbative effects arising from short-range correlations and their role in the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations have significant nonperturbative effects on the Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to the orbital Hall effect.
motivation: Previous calculations of the orbital magnetic moment omitted a Berry connection term; this work aims to provide a rigorous derivation and assess its impact on the orbital Hall effect.
method: The authors derive matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment including the Berry connection term, and compute the orbital Hall conductivity for a model system.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital Hall conductivity in certain materials, highlighting the need for its inclusion.
conclusion: The corrected orbital magnetic moment formula is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Hamiltonians Using The Sorted-list Encoding
authors: Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Calvin Ku, Yu-Cheng Chen, Alice Hu, and Min-Hsiu Hsieh

Quantum phase estimation is a cornerstone algorithm for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for electronic structure calculations of chemical systems. Optimal simulation relies on a complex trade-offs across many parameters including Hamiltonian simulation techniques, basis sets, and the …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033091] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Benchmarks quantum simulation of chemical Hamiltonians using sorted-list encoding for phase estimation.
motivation: To optimize quantum simulation for chemical systems by evaluating different encoding and simulation techniques.
method: Compares sorted-list encoding with other methods in terms of gate count and circuit depth for Hamiltonian simulation.
result: Sorted-list encoding reduces resource requirements for certain Hamiltonians but overall contribution is incremental.
conclusion: The paper is a benchmarking study without novel theoretical or algorithmic advances in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in quasiperiodic systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors investigate two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, analyzing the quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and interlayer hybridization effects.
conclusion: The work contributes to the physics of quasiperiodic lattices but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the SSH model, comparing three diagnostics.
motivation: Topological phases are typically defined at zero temperature, but realistic systems operate at finite temperature, so understanding how topology manifests in mixed states is important.
method: The authors compute the ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body topological invariant for the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension at nonzero temperature.
result: They find that the ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined and captures topological features, while the other diagnostics have limitations.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a useful indicator of topology in mixed states, but the study is specific to non-interacting models and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter Equation For Open Systems: Emergence Of Exceptional Points In Excitonic Spectra From First Principles
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, And Gianluca Stefanucci
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenlin Zhang, Wei Hu, Enrico Perfetto, and Gianluca Stefanucci

Extension of the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems predicts that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides, providing a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031020] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the Bethe-Salpeter equation to open quantum systems, predicting exceptional points in excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides for non-Hermitian quantum devices.
motivation: To understand and control excitonic properties in open quantum systems for novel optical and valleytronic devices.
method: They develop a non-Hermitian Bethe-Salpeter equation from first principles to model excitons in open systems coupled to photonic environments.
result: They find that engineered photonic environments induce exceptional points in the excitonic spectra of transition-metal dichalcogenides.
conclusion: This provides a pathway for non-Hermitian quantum devices with controllable optical and valleytronic properties.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang
